findings.title: Retry cleanup deletes WorkflowReminders of any method
findings.body: The deleteMany query uses OR with a second condition that only checks retryCount > 1. This deletes every WorkflowReminder row with retryCount > 1, not just unscheduled SMS reminders. Since retryCount is on the shared WorkflowReminder table, EMAIL/WHATSAPP reminders or scheduled SMS rows that ever have retryCount > 1 can be deleted. Scope the retry cleanup to method: WorkflowMethods.SMS and likely scheduled: false.

findings.title: Retry count is incremented from a stale value
findings.body: Both failure paths (lines 184 and 195) set retryCount to reminder.retryCount + 1 using the value read before the SMS attempt. If two cron executions process the same reminder, or if the row is updated between the read and write, increments can be lost or applied incorrectly, preventing deletion after two failures. Use Prisma's atomic increment and guard the update for unscheduled reminders.

findings.title: Retry update in catch can abort the whole cron handler
findings.body: The catch block awaits prisma.workflowReminder.update to increment retryCount. If that update fails, for example because the reminder was deleted after the initial findMany or due to a DB error, the exception is not caught and will terminate the loop, leaving remaining reminders unprocessed. The same applies to the failure-path update. Use updateMany or wrap the retry increment in its own try/catch and ignore not-found errors.

findings.title: No tests for the new retry/deletion behavior
findings.body: The PR introduces a retry counter and deletes reminders after repeated SMS scheduling failures, but no automated tests verify that retryCount is incremented on failure, that reminders are deleted only after the intended number of failures, and that non-SMS reminders are unaffected. This logic is prone to regressions.
